newsitem.title: UK: No UK plan to revamp investment rules - Knight.
newsitem.headline: No UK plan to revamp investment rules - Knight.

text.p: Britain has no intention of completely changing its regulations of the financial industry just because of a few problems in the past, Treasury Minister Angela Knight said on Wednesday.
"No system can offer a copper-bottomed guarantee that no investor will lose," she told a conference on recently-launched open-ended investment companies (OEICs).
"Last year saw a few problems. It is clear that no wholesale revision of regulation is required to prevent a recurrence of what was an isolated incident," she said.

The fund industry in Britain was rocked last year after revelations last year of misvaluations in three of the funds run by Morgan Grenfell Asset Management and subsequent sacking of fund manager Peter Young.
Young, who denies any criminal activity, is being investigated by Britain's Serious Fraud Office.
"However, the regulators have been consulting about whether there is a need to make some minor changes to the unit trust regulations," Knight said.
The government is now looking to what she called the next generation of OEICs and hoped to make progress soon.
Regulations for these investment companies came into force earlier this month, aimed at allowing UK managers to capture for London some of the the European mutual fund business.

Much of the fund management of Luxembourg and Dublin based funds is already done in London, underlining the need for Britain to have a mutual investment fund which could be understood by foreign investors, Knight said.
